title: Business Requirements Document — New Requirements Chat

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body:
Audit of 'AI-Driven Requirement Engineering Assistant1 (1).pdf' (Project Name- AI-Driven Requirement Engineering Assistant) — Domain: ECOMMERCE: Extracted 2073 words across 171 requirement statements. The document establishes functional scope but requires formal PCI-DSS, GDPR/CCPA (customer PII) compliance definitions, API contracts, and security hardening.

This Business Requirements Document establishes the foundational business vision, target capabilities, and operational value propositions for **New Requirements Chat**.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body:
• **Primary Objective**: Deliver enterprise-ready functionality for New Requirements Chat while guaranteeing PCI-DSS, GDPR/CCPA (customer PII) compliance.
• **Operational Goal**: Provide end-to-end requirement traceability across all delivery stages.
• **Target Success Metrics**: 100% test coverage for critical business paths; zero unresolved high-severity compliance gaps.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries
sections.body:
• **In Scope**: Ingestion, validation, and execution of functional paths specified for New Requirements Chat; automated compliance audit against PCI-DSS, GDPR/CCPA (customer PII).
• **Out of Scope**: Unspecified legacy hardware adapters; non-standard external integrations not defined in source documentation.

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body:
1. **Enterprise Product Sponsor**: Approves strategic requirements and business scope.
2. **Lead Solutions Architect**: Validates domain architecture for ECOMMERCE industry standards.
3. **Compliance & Security Auditor**: Enforces adherence to PCI-DSS, GDPR/CCPA (customer PII).
4. **Lead QA Engineer**: Certifies acceptance criteria and RTM coverage.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body:
• **Compliance Constraint**: System must enforce PCI-DSS, GDPR/CCPA (customer PII) safeguards at all data boundaries.
• **NFR Benchmarks**: cart consistency under concurrent stock updates, P95 checkout latency < 300ms.
• **Identified Gaps**: ECOMMERCE Regulatory Compliance & Security Controls (PCI-DSS, GDPR/CCPA (customer PII)), Non-Functional Requirements (NFR): SLAs & Throughput, Data Architecture & Schema Definitions

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body:
• **[HIGH Risk] High Ambiguity & Untestable Language (Project Name- AI-Driven Requirement Engineering Assistant)**: Specification contains subjective and untestable phrasing including 'fast'. Engineering teams cannot derive deterministic acceptance tests. *(Mitigation: Rewrite requirements into verifiable Gherkin syntax (Given/When/Then) with quantifiable metrics (e.g. latency, error rates).)*
• **[HIGH Risk] ECOMMERCE Data Protection & PCI-DSS Compliance Gap**: Document specifies financial transactions or payments without defining PCI-DSS, GDPR/CCPA (customer PII) tokenization, webhook verification, or idempotent charge safety. *(Mitigation: Integrate certified payment gateway with client-side tokenization (e.g., Stripe Elements) and zero plain-text card data retention.)*

File: A Hospital Management System.pdf
--- Page 1 ---
Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
